youtube_title: Munster, Indiana: the Brass Tavern fire and the house behind it
youtube:
You asked for Munster! "This is my bedroom. Get out." A ghost tour operator says a voice once whispered that inside a house in Munster, Indiana. The house stands behind the spot where the Brass Tavern stood, an old inn on Ridge Road. A new family bought it in 1864. Their daughter later wrote that it housed the region's only telegraph office, and that news of Lincoln's assassination first reached the area there. In the fall of 1909, the old tavern burned. She wrote that the beams smoldered for days. Her family built a new house behind the ruins. Today it's a museum in Heritage Park. One haunted-places listing reports footsteps, cold spots, and a presence in the bedroom. That part is legend. The fire was real. Comment your town, and it could be next! #Munster #MunsterIndiana #LakeCountyIndiana #TheRegion #Haunted #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Wilhelmine Stallbohm Kaske, 'Early Days in Munster' (History of Lake County, 1934); National Register of Historic Places nomination, Stallbohm Barn-Kaske House (1996); Brass Tavern / Kaske House historical marker (2023). The ghost reports: Mike McDowell of Indiana Ghost Trackers in GreatNews.Life; HauntedPlaces.org (user-submitted). More local history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
